axiom-crave: Straight, accurate and sneakily far for its speed. Flight shifts a lot between copies.
westside-harp: Fades like it has somewhere to be. Steady in wind, short on glide.
innova-wraith: Big forehand distance and sweet glide once seasoned. Owners keep buying it in new plastics.
kastaplast-berg: Lands and sits by the basket like a well-trained dog. Wind barely bothers it.
innova-mako3: Very straight and honest. It holds your exact release, so it tattles on every mistake.
axiom-hex: Straight, predictable mid with a low-profile grip that sits comfortably in the hand.
innova-teebird3: Workhorse fairway with a straight flight and fade. New ones arrive with some attitude.
mvp-wave: Easy distance on hyzer flips and turnovers at moderate arm speeds. Light Fission copies flip fast.
mvp-trail: Easy glide and distance for modest arms. Every run seems to have its own personality.
mvp-detour: Flips up, drifts right and threads forehand gaps. Basically a Hex's more adventurous cousin.
streamline-pilot: Shallow, comfortable putter with a straight, glidey flight that also handles approaches.
mvp-reactor: Slightly overstable mid with a dependable fade and serious torque resistance on forehands.
latitude-64-pure: Holds whatever line it gets and feels great in hand. Opto for throwing, Zero for putting.
mvp-resistor: A slower baby Firebird for forehands, utility shots and wind. Some runs are pure beef.
mvp-tesla: More overstable than its numbers admit. New copies hook like they owe the ground money.
latitude-64-river: Loads of glide and easy distance for slower arms. Turns over once you add power.
latitude-64-fuse: Straight, glidey understable mid that flips flat and threads tight wooded lines.
mvp-volt: Beefy fairway with a dependable fade for forehands and wind. Plenty of copies run short.
axiom-envy: Accurate throwing putter with a comfy grip and surprising distance. Gets flippy as it wears.
discraft-zone: Overstable approach disc with a fade so predictable you could set your watch by it.
prodigy-pa-5: Shallow, flippy putter with lovely glide for turnovers and hyzer flips. Easy for beginners too.
thought-space-athletics-construct: Long, controllable distance with plenty of glide. Copies and plastics can fly noticeably differently.
westside-hatchet: Flippy, glidey driver for turnovers and hyzer flips. Some copies secretly want to be rollers.
innova-gator: Very overstable mid with a trusty finish for upshots, wind and forehands. Glide not included.
innova-wombat3: Holds almost any line with lots of glide. Trees will need a better plan.
westside-king: A fast disc that actually turns over, with huge distance. Often flippy enough to roll.
axiom-paradox: Very understable specialty mid for turnovers, hyzer flips and rollers. Not an every-hole disc.
discmania-origin: Smooth, understable mid with good glide and a comfy feel. Gets flippier with wear.
discraft-hades: Long, understable driver that fades back hard. The line between turnover and roller is thin.
discraft-luna: Accurate putter that holds lines and sails surprisingly far. The deep rim isn't for every hand.
innova-corvette: Long throws, lots of glide, reliable fade. A fair-weather friend, so skip it on windy days.
mvp-uplink: Glidey turnover mid for woods shots and drifting right. Friendly for beginners, burns out with power.
westside-anvil: Meathook approach disc for skips, flex shots and escaping trouble. Your get-out-of-jail card.
innova-jay: Straight, stable mid that resists turning. It just doesn't share the Mako3's love of gliding.
kastaplast-berg-x: A more stable Berg with a comfy feel, built for approaches that need to stick.
mvp-inertia: Long driver, often more stable than its numbers say. Handles hyzer flips and turnovers.
mvp-nomad: Deep-rimmed putter with a bead and a lovely feel. Firm plastics can get slippery.
axiom-fireball: Built for wind, skips and hooking corners. Turning over is not on the menu.
discmania-md3: Point-and-shoot mid with a reliable fade. Trust it not to turn over on you.
discmania-pd: Overstable control driver that stays in play and fades back. Beating it in takes some patience.
discraft-buzzz-ss: Slightly understable, predictable mid for forehand flicks and shorter shots. Safe for beginners.
dynamic-discs-emac-truth: Straight, dependable mid that holds lines. It has quietly evicted Buzzzes and Hexes from bags.
innova-aviar3: Straight, fairly overstable putter with a reliable fade, great for throwing and forehands.
innova-tl: Point-and-throw fairway that flies true to its numbers. Out of production, so hoard wisely.
streamline-drift: Flies close to its numbers with easy hyzer flips. Gains turn with use.
innova-fox: Turns over easily with loads of glide, made for hyzer flips and wooded lines.
latitude-64-diamond: Light, glidey and very understable, often the disc behind a first drive worth bragging about.
latitude-64-explorer: Mild, reliable fade on a straight, stable fairway that holds lines and shrugs off wind.
latitude-64-maul: Glidey, understable driver with easy hyzer flips. Often more predictable than a River.
mvp-entropy: Zone-like approach putter, often a touch less stable. Plastic matters a lot here.
mvp-ion: Lovely feel and bead. Plenty of throwers have made it their main putter for years.
prodigy-a5: Straight to stable approach disc, like a Zone with more glide. Strong on forehands.
westside-stag: Glidey, straight fairway with a reliable fade. Often more understable than its numbers.
prodigy-m4: Glidey, comfortable mid that holds lines and loves hyzer flips through the woods.
mvp-anode: Straight-line putter with grippy options. Wet Proton feels like holding a bar of soap.
westside-warship: Very glidey mid with fairway-like distance that holds lines, great on wooded courses.
axiom-pixel: Glidey putter for longer putts and straight throws. The shallow dome divides hands.
innova-beast: Long, accurate driver that sticks around for years. Each tree hit makes it a little flippier.
innova-invader: Straight, grippy putter and approach disc with a shallow profile. Point and shoot, even in wind.
innova-tern: Adds real length for plenty of arms, slower ones included, with easy turnovers.
prodigy-a3: Beefy, overstable approach disc with a great rim and grip, especially strong for long forehands.
westside-sword: Long, mostly straight distance driver. Stability swings a lot across plastics, weights and runs.
innova-roadrunner: Does hyzer flips, turnovers and slow S-turns with ease. Star flips, Halo and Champion hold.
discmania-fd: Straight, reliable fairway with a gentle fade. C-Line runs beefier, S-Line flips with wear.
innova-wolf: Popular first disc for anhyzer lines. Beats in fast, so the honeymoon can be short.
latitude-64-saint: Glidey, easy distance and a favorite for learning hyzer flips. Wind exposes its understable side.
axiom-rhythm: Far-flying, forgiving fairway for hyzer flips and forehands, though it gets flippy fast with wear.
discmania-essence: Long, very glidey fairway that gives near-max distance without a big arm.
innova-orc: Straight, controllable distance driver that throwers keep for years. Tree hits can soften it.
prodigy-pa-3: Shallow-rimmed putter with a small bead and comfy feel. Stability and feel shift between runs.
axiom-pyro: Overstable mid that comes out clean on forehands and fades reliably. Laughs at wind.
innova-mamba: Long hyzer flips and low-ceiling shots. Heavy Star copies sometimes forget they're understable.
mvp-watt: Straight, floaty throwing putter that holds lines. Neutron can turn slick in cold air.
streamline-trace: Long, straight driver often compared to a Wraith. Lighter copies turn flippy at full power.
mvp-relay: Fairway for hyzer flips and tight wooded lines. Copies range widely, from beefy to flippy.
streamline-range: Glidey approach and putting disc that many prefer to a Berg. Turns over when thrown hard.
mvp-photon: Overstable driver with a reliable fade for forehands. Often beefier than advertised out of the box.
kastaplast-svea: A touchy, shape-it mid that glides forever at low power. Muscle it and it flips.
kastaplast-reko: Grip and feel win fans in K3 and K1 Soft. K1 can get slick when damp.
innova-teebird: Straight flight, reliable fade, years of service. Basically the old pickup truck of fairways.
axiom-insanity: Long, fairly understable driver for hyzer flips. Plastics and runs fly very differently.
mvp-atom: Comfortable and shallow, this putter flies straight and throws nicely on approaches too.
kastaplast-kaxe: Midrange with fairway-like distance and a reliable fade. Stability depends on which run you grab.
kastaplast-jarn: Fades reliably and sits right where it lands. A forehand favorite, often replacing a Zone.
innova-destroyer: Go-to overstable driver for distance, forehands and headwinds. Needs a strong arm, and runs vary.
mvp-servo: A slightly more stable Crave with reliable, straight flights and easy hyzer flips.
latitude-64-grace: Long, glidey driver often compared to a Wraith. Runs and editions range from beefy to flippy.
innova-roc3: Straight mid with a reliable fade, offered in plastics for different stability needs.
innova-toro: An approach disc with extra bite over a Zone. Drops like it just remembered gravity.
prodigy-a2: Forehand flex shots love its dependable fade. Stays overstable for ages, but dumps quickly.
westside-tursas: Easy, beginner-friendly mid for turnovers and hyzer flips. Hard throws make it flip.
kastaplast-falk: Flies flippy new and grows more stable with wear, which is backwards in the best way.
axiom-tempo: Straight, forgiving low-speed disc for forehand approaches, with a gentle fade to finish.
discraft-buzzz: Neutral, reliable mid that holds lines and fades gently. Forgiving and easy to shape.
innova-valkyrie: Friendly to developing arms with good glide. Beats in fast, then turns over like it's tired.
discraft-cicada: Understable, glidey and straight-flying, with a thin rim that feels great in hand.
latitude-64-ballista-pro: Big distance and solid in headwinds. Gold runs overstable, while Opto and beat-in copies flip.
mvp-orbital: Swooping lines and rollers are its thing. Its flight numbers read more like wishful thinking.
discraft-athena: Controllable, accurate fairway that flies like a stable Teebird, even when you swing hard.
innova-aviarx3: Notably overstable putter for approaches, forehands and headwinds, with a comfy shallow rim.
innova-rollo: A very understable specialty tool built for rollers, turnovers and hyzer flips.
discmania-dd3: Glidey distance driver that often outflies a Destroyer for slower arms. Soft versions beat in fast.
innova-hawkeye: A staple in plenty of bags, this controllable fairway can flip more once broken in.
latitude-64-compass: Straight, neutral mid that holds its line with a soft finish. Easy for forehands and beginners.
streamline-echo: Forgiving, line-holding mid, like a straighter Hex. Complaints are about as rare as an ace.
westside-bear: Stable, glidey fairway with a reliable finish and comfy rim. Runs vary in dome.
kastaplast-reko-x: Overstable throwing putter that fits the hand and sticks around in bags long-term.
kastaplast-stig: A mid with fairway ambitions, and it often gets there. Runs understable and a bit inconsistent.
mvp-octane: Often the longest driver in the bag. Some Neutron copies play hard to turn.
mvp-signal: Easy, understable fairway for hyzer flips and turnover lines on wooded courses.
thought-space-athletics-praxis: A straight, glidey throwing putter. Powered upshots may sail past the basket and wave goodbye.
westside-maiden: Throwers often pick firmer plastic for putting and VIP for throwing. Straight and glidey.
discmania-fd3: Overstable fast driver with hard fades for forehands and wind, often likened to a Firebird.
discraft-scorch: Feel, glide and fade, if the right copy finds you. Every Scorch is a mystery box.
dynamic-discs-trespass: Go-to distance driver with plenty of glide, in Destroyer and Wraith territory. Loosens up with wear.
innova-nova: Neutral, straight putter that holds angles, great for form work. The deep rim can catch fingers.
innova-whale: A dependable putter that throwers stick with for years. Holds lines well.
discraft-anax: Glide and wind handling show up once it's beaten in. Holds a line and fades reliably.
discraft-buzzz-os: Firm finishes for forehands and wind. Might overlap with discs already crowding your bag.
discraft-heat: Understable driver for forehands, turnovers and easy distance. Strong arms may find it too turny.
prodigy-f1: Accurate, predictable overstable fairway for forehands and headwinds. Wear can turn it flippy fast.
prodigy-m2: Dependable go-to mid with a straight to gently overstable flight. Holds up to heavy play.
westside-bard: Flat, glidey mid with a dependable fade for shots that must not turn over.
westside-destiny: Less stable than its speed suggests, so it hyzer flips far. Headwinds are its kryptonite.
discraft-avenger-ss: Flippy driver that holds a turnover and loves hyzer flips, though it wears in quickly.
discraft-banger-gt: Comfy thumb groove and a straight flight inside the circle. Glide clocks out a little early.
discraft-raptor: Overstable, easy-to-control fairway for forehands and wind. Runs range from very beefy to straight.
discraft-sol: Glidey hybrid that holds a turn at low power. With muscle, it runs out of steam.
discraft-undertaker: Holds turnovers once broken in, with a straight flight and gentle fade.
innova-daedalus: Turns and burns with big S-curves, which some arms love and others argue with.
innova-racer: Glidey driver with a narrow S-curve and great distance. Handles wind and suits forehands.
innova-skeeter: A classic first disc that slips through short tunnels like it knows a shortcut.
latitude-64-culverin: Mostly straight and controllable, with a dependable fade. Forehand friendly and fine in headwinds.
latitude-64-glory: A slow, glidey fairway that's beefier than an Explorer. Takes ages to beat in.
latitude-64-mercy: Comfy, shallow putter with a true line and a touch of fade. Zero softens in heat.
latitude-64-strive: Flippier than its numbers, so it flies far without a big arm. A hyzer-flip cruise missile.
westside-crown: Shallow, glidey beaded putter that floats a long way, so putts can sail long.
westside-northman: Turnover S-lines, hyzer flips and escaping the rough, all from a slightly understable driver.
westside-sampo: Glidey, overstable driver for flex shots and headwinds. Dumps late, and Elasto softens in heat.
discmania-link: Neutral beaded putter with a comfy grip and little fade. Glides less than a P2.
discmania-mutant: Extremely overstable mid that never turns over. Asking it to fly straight is a lost cause.
discraft-fierce: Fierce by name, soft by nature. Holds its line and leans understable on long upshots.
discraft-thrasher: Rises from a hyzer, glides long and fades back. Plastic and weight change things.
discraft-zone-os: Beefier than most approach discs, which is saying something. Wind and flex shots, handled.
dynamic-discs-maverick: Easy-to-control fairway that holds lines through woods and tunnels. Becomes a staple fast.
innova-eagle: Dependable overstable fairway with a reliable fade, steady in wind and lovely on forehand.
innova-tl3: Holds hyzer or anhyzer lines dead straight, then fades gently. Great in tight woods.
innova-thunderbird: Neutral to overstable fairway with a reliable fade that beats in nicely. Needs some power.
innova-firebird: Hard-fading utility driver. The fade is less a suggestion and more a court order.
axiom-proxy: Predictable, shallow putter that suits smaller hands. Release it on hyzer or it may flip.
innova-leopard: Forgiving fairway that starts as a learner disc and grows into a hyzer-flip go-to.
latitude-64-claymore: Glidey, accurate mid with little fade, often compared to a Buzzz. Handles tunnels and wind.
mvp-glitch: Fun, glidey putter with almost no fade, so it won't correct mistakes. Great for scramble shots.
innova-pig: Forehand approach putter that flies straight and sits down like it found a mud puddle.
innova-shryke: Long forehand bombs for open fields. Keep it to wide spaces, unless disc hunting sounds fun.
mvp-deflector: Skips, scrambles and windy days are its job. Will probably outlast your bag.
innova-sidewinder: Forehand shaping and hyzer flips come easy. Runs swing a lot in stability.
innova-leopard3: Accurate, mildly understable fairway for hyzer flips. Gets flippy as power grows or it beats in.
innova-rat: Shallow approach disc with a gentle fade that fills the gap between putter and mid.
kastaplast-lots: Smooth and glidey with surprising distance through woods and wind. Stability depends on plastic and run.
latitude-64-saint-pro: Glidey fairway with a reliable fade that suits newer throwers. Beats in fast toward understable.
mvp-matrix: Handles power and torque with a dependable fade. Your Reactor might get a little jealous.
innova-caiman: Little glide and a dependable dump make it a forehand and wind specialist for approaches.
westside-underworld: A friendly first distance disc that turns over easily. Rollers practically throw themselves.
axiom-bokeh: Think slightly more stable Crave, long and glidey. The Latte run brings a harder fade.
innova-gorgon: Comfy and very glidey, with easy distance. Some copies turn over enough to make you dizzy.
streamline-lift: Grippy, easy-to-turn driver for newer throwers and hyzer flips. Eclipse copies are all over the map.
innova-rhyno: Overstable putter that resists wind and torque. Premium plastics stay beefy longer.
innova-roc: Controllable mid that keeps improving as it beats in, ending up a hyzer-flip or dead-straight gem.
kastaplast-gote: Slow, glidey and dead straight through tunnels. It's picky about how you hold it.
discraft-passion: A longer, Buzzz-style fairway that holds whatever line it's given. Dependably straight.
latitude-64-ballista: Far more understable than its numbers. In calm air with the right arm, it flies forever.
axiom-balance: Stays straight for most of the flight, then pushes into a reliable fade.
discmania-p2: Long-loved putter for putting, approaches and throwing. Resists turning over, year after year.
dynamic-discs-felon: Overstable fairway for forehands, headwinds and hard fades. Lucid beats in straighter.
dynamic-discs-justice: Torque resistant and comfy to grip, with a firm finish on forehands and in wind.
innova-xcaliber: Late fade for flex lines, and Star versions mellow within months.
innova-yeti-aviar: Soft, grippy putter that loves rain and cold, as a Yeti should. Gets gummy in summer.
streamline-jet: High-speed and very understable, for turnovers, tailwinds and rollers. Flat releases get twitchy.
streamline-runway: A long straight runway before a dependable fade. Cleared for landing, forehand or backhand.
axiom-virus: On the right angle it's long and accurate. Otherwise it turns a lot and fights back.
discmania-instinct: Controllable fairway with a gentle fade, often likened to a Teebird. Neo can turn over.
discraft-meteor: Workable, flippy mid for hyzer flips and turnovers. Z versions range from flippy to barely turning.
dynamic-discs-escape: Good glide and a fade that comes back. Great for slower arms and newer throwers.
streamline-ascend: Easy to turn over and fun for shaping lines, with plenty of glide.
streamline-flare: Firebird energy with extra glide. Fades so hard it occasionally tries to dig for treasure.
westside-pine: The only Pine on the course worth aiming at. Glidey, with a slow, dependable fade.
axiom-time-lapse: In beefy Destroyer territory, though plenty of throwers found it short on glide.
discmania-md1: Dead-straight mid with barely any fade. Lines come out like they were drawn with a ruler.
dynamic-discs-judge: Comfortable, predictable putter for putts, approaches and tee shots. Easy to commit to.
innova-dragon: Light, understable beginner driver for hyzer flips. It floats in water, which ponds hate.
kastaplast-malm: Glidey, controllable fast fairway with a nice fade and real distance. Less torque resistant.
latitude-64-rive: Headwinds and forehand flex lines suit this overstable driver, at least until it wears in.
latitude-64-trident: Versatile control mid, especially in Gold Line. Tree hits can make it unpredictable.
mvp-control: Flies like a beefier Trail, best thrown flat or on anhyzer. Can fade early.
prodigy-f3: Understable-to-straight fairway for hyzer flips and gentle S-curves. Copies fly differently.
discraft-wasp: A Buzzz with a bit more sting. Straight flight, dependable fade, forehand friendly.
dynamic-discs-deputy: Glidey, slightly understable putter that holds its line. Long putts can drift.
innova-mystere: Flies straight to understable and serves as a go-to for plenty. GStar and Halo flip more.
kastaplast-vass: A flip-up bomber that fades back. In strong wind it just shrugs and quits.
latitude-64-bolt: Big hyzers and slower arms suit this long, understable driver. Often too flippy for power.
latitude-64-brave: Flippy, far-flying fairway with a reliable fade back, great for newer throwers.
latitude-64-xxx: Overstable utility driver for tomahawks and thumbers. Some love it too much to risk losing it.
prodigy-a4: Low-profile, glidey putter for forehands and shaping shots. The whistle splits the room.
prodigy-f2: Forehand-friendly fairway with a straight flight and late fade. Copies vary from beefy to flippy.
thought-space-athletics-mana: Understable mid with Buzzz-like feel. Reviews glow so bright they need sunglasses.
discmania-method: Versatile, grippy mid for throwers who enjoy the slow art of beating in a disc.
innova-atlas: Floaty, accurate mid with good grip, often compared to a Buzzz. Release consistency matters.
innova-lion: Torque-resistant midrange with a gentle, reliable fade. Dependable on approaches and in wind.
innova-polecat: Accurate and very straight, though missed putts sometimes go on a little rollaway adventure.
innova-savant: Stable fairway for hyzers, headwinds and woods shots. Thunderbird owners may find overlap.
kastaplast-idog: Reliable fade, solid in wind, and it outflies comparable speeds. A favorite fairway for plenty.
axiom-mayhem: Flies very far and forehand throwers love it. Plasma runs beefy, Neutron flips.
discmania-md4: Loved for its reliable fade in wind and on forehand. Finishes a bit dumpy.
discraft-malta: Less glide than a Roc3, with a reliable fade for forehands and hyzers.
discraft-zone-ss: Workable, understable forehand putter. On touch shots it can be a bit overenthusiastic.
dynamic-discs-verdict: Comfortable overstable mid with a secure grip, friendly for forehands and beginners.
dynamic-discs-warden: Comfortable, versatile putter for putting and drives. Base plastic flips when beaten in.
prodigy-d1: Far, accurate distance driver for forehand anhyzers. Runs range from stable to flippy.
prodigy-d3: Effortless distance for hyzer flips and turnovers. Goes understable quickly as it beats in.
discmania-dd: Little fade, long hyzer flips and easy turnovers. Wind exposes the flippy copies.
discmania-logic: Mostly loved for how it sits in the hand. A line-holding putter with some glide.
discraft-archer: Slow, understable fairway for turnovers, anhyzers and forehands. A good first disc to turn over.
dynamic-discs-sheriff: Controllable go-to distance driver with a consistent fade. Full power can turn it over.
dynamic-discs-vandal: Big anhyzers and turnovers are its specialty. Glidey, controllable, and flippier with wear.
innova-sync: Line-holding, fairly straight throwing putter that handles forehands but loses stability quickly.
kastaplast-guld: Forehand bombers love it. Holds a hyzer flip and fades dependably.
kastaplast-stal: Controllable overstable driver with a soft fade, often picked over a Firebird. Light on glide.
latitude-64-havoc: Fast, understable and far with a slight fade. Even the complaints say it flies too far.
latitude-64-raketen: Real distance and some control in wind. Turns over and beats in quickly.
latitude-64-sinus: Overstable driving putter that starts beefy and seasons straighter. The thumb track divides opinion.
mvp-impulse: Easy, forgiving driver that turns and hyzer flips without asking much. Doubles as a roller.
mvp-phase: Wind and utility driver with plenty of beef, handy for forehand rollers and skips.
prodigy-archive: Stable mid with a strong fade that stands tall in headwinds. Comfortable in hand.
prodigy-d2: Long, consistent driver. The old chalky copies get treated like vintage wine.
thought-space-athletics-coalesce: Fairly overstable fairway that pushes straight, handles wind and beats into a workhorse.
westside-vellamo: Holds its line even when your release doesn't. Warship and Buzzz vibes, little fade.
innova-boss: Wind-proof, very overstable distance driver, though certain copies are total meat hooks.
innova-dart: Accurate, controllable throwing putter. The domey shape feels odd until suddenly it doesn't.
mvp-dimension: Stable to overstable driver that flies far and handles wind. Can flip as it beats in.
mvp-ohm: Stable, very straight throwing putter that holds its line. Some find it too stable to shape shots.
mvp-spin: Grippy even when wet, this straight, understable putter handles turn shots. Cold, dry hands may slip.
axiom-vanish: Straight, long and reliable at the finish. Some copies won't flip, no matter how nicely asked.
discmania-md5: Handles any power, shot shape or wind, forehand or backhand. A dependable overstable mid.
discmania-rainmaker: Feel and glide win praise, and it's beefier than an Aviar. Grip can slip for some.
discraft-drone: Driver-like overstable mid with a floaty line and hard fade. Z is beefier than ESP FLX.
discraft-force: Goes left reliably and often wins the overstable slot over a Destroyer. Z is the beefiest.
dynamic-discs-suspect: Shallow, straight mid that flies like a comfier Harp or Zone, forehand or backhand.
innova-archangel: Flippy and fun, great for slower arms. DX plastic gets flippier fast.
innova-colt: A putter that drives farther than most of its putter friends. XT is the crowd favorite.
innova-invictus: Basically a faster Firebird. Beefy, overstable and solid in headwinds.
innova-mirage: Shallow, understable putter with lots of glide for long putts, flips and anhyzers.
innova-rocx3: Consistent fade on forehand and backhand, even in wind. Controllable and overstable.
innova-shark: Easy, predictable mid that throwers keep for years. DX plastic beats in.
kastaplast-nord: Moderately overstable mid between a Roc3 and a Harp, with decent glide and wind handling.
kastaplast-alva: Long-flying, flippy driver that needs room. Turnovers are its happy place.
latitude-64-sapphire: Beefy when new with an aggressive finish. Give it time and it calms right down.
latitude-64-trust: Glidey, comfy workhorse mid, though throwers can't agree on its stability.
mvp-catalyst: Neutral workhorse with big distance when the release is right. After months it wants more hyzer.
streamline-stabilizer: Reliably overstable, flat-profile disc that takes the stress out of short approaches.
westside-shield: Tacky putter that grips the chains and won't let go. Wears fast but keeps its stability.
